name: beautiful-qt
description: Write, review, port, and enforce idiomatic Qt 6 desktop applications in C++20: three skills distilled from the Qt 6 documentation, the Widgets/Quick guidance, and the facta desktop handbook, plus a drop-in clang-tidy and clang-format config.

interface.longDescription:
Three skills for Qt 6 desktop developers on C++20, distilled from the Qt 6 documentation, the Widgets/Quick guidance, and the facta desktop handbook.

qt-best-practices guides new desktop code: the sacred GUI thread, QFuture/QtConcurrent and worker threads, the domain/application/adapter/presentation/platform layers, MVVM with bindable QObject ViewModels and QAbstractItemModel, ownership and QObject lifetimes, the C++ SDK and realtime ports, SQLite and the outbox, signed updates, accessibility and the low-end performance budget.

qt-review reviews a Widgets/QML screen, ViewModel, model, thread boundary, SDK/SQLite adapter, CMake target graph, or diff and returns a prioritized report. Architecture and GUI-thread contracts rank above everything. Every finding cites a file and line, the rule it breaks, and the smallest fix.

qt-port ports Qt 5, QML-only, PySide/PyQt, Electron, or a web screen to Qt 6 C++ with the same behavior. It ports the original tests first and writes a PORTING.md.

The skills contain instructions and reference text only. They make no network calls and collect no data. When a Qt/C++ toolchain is available, the skills run CMake, ctest, clang-format, and clang-tidy on your project; without one, they work from the code alone. A drop-in clang-tidy and clang-format config is available in the GitHub repository.
capabilities: Review Qt code with cited rules
Port Qt 5, QML, PySide or web screens to Qt 6
defaultPrompt: Review this Qt window and list what to fix first
Port this PySide screen to idiomatic C++ Qt 6
Move this blocking call off the GUI thread

publication.release_notes: Initial release: three Qt 6 skills, the layer and GUI-thread contract, and a proven clang-tidy config.
